essentialIdeas: Phospholipids form a bilayer with hydrophilic heads outward and hydrophobic tails inward, so small nonpolar molecules pass more easily than charged or polar ones.
Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.

activities.label: Membrane structure model
activities.title: Phospholipid bilayer and permeability
activities.body: Read the model and note the two structural parts that control what crosses. Then move on to the first check.

essentialIdeas: Phospholipids form a bilayer with hydrophilic heads outward and hydrophobic tails inward, so small nonpolar molecules pass more easily than charged or polar ones.
Passive transport moves substances down a concentration gradient without cellular energy, while active transport uses energy to move substances against the gradient.

activities.label: Explain membrane selectivity
activities.title: Explain selective permeability
activities.body: In your own words, explain why the bilayer lets some substances cross more easily than others. Then submit your explanation.
activities.correctAnswer: The hydrophilic heads face water and the hydrophobic interior blocks charged or polar substances, so small nonpolar molecules cross more easily.
activities.feedback: A complete answer links bilayer structure to what can cross. If needed, add that the hydrophobic interior is the key barrier.

activities.label: Fix the transport rule
activities.title: Repair transport distinction
activities.body: If you mixed up transport direction or energy use, correct it here. State the rule in one clear sentence.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Confusing passive transport with active transport by treating both as energy-requiring movement.
activities.correctAnswer: Passive transport moves down a concentration gradient without energy, and active transport requires energy to move against the gradient.
activities.feedback: Repair the energy rule and the direction rule together. Passive is downhill and does not use cellular energy; active is uphill and does use energy.

activities.label: State the model again
activities.title: Reexplain membrane transport
activities.body: Explain the whole membrane model again from memory in plain language. Keep it brief and specific.
activities.correctAnswer: The phospholipid bilayer makes the membrane selectively permeable, and transport can be passive when substances move down a gradient or active when the cell uses energy to move against it.
activities.feedback: Your answer should connect structure, permeability, and the two transport directions. A strong response names both passive and active correctly.

activities.label: Check transport classification
activities.title: Which transport is this?
activities.body: Choose the best classification for the example and submit one answer.
choices: A molecule moves from high concentration to low concentration without cellular energy.
A molecule moves from low concentration to high concentration using cellular energy.
A molecule stays inside the membrane and never crosses.
A molecule changes into a different substance before crossing.
activities.correctAnswer: A molecule moves from low concentration to high concentration using cellular energy.
activities.feedback: Active transport requires energy and moves against the concentration gradient. The other choices describe no transport, passive transport, or an unrelated change.
